en: The Philippines officially consists of 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of them have people living on them.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is unique because it sits on Volcano Island, which is located inside Taal Lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine Tarsier in Bohol has enormous eyes that are each individually larger than its entire brain.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by hand over 2,000 years ago.
Lake Mainit in Surigao del Norte is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a depth of 223 meters.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching for 505 kilometers.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine Trench contains the Galathea Depth, which is the deepest point in the Philippine Sea at 10,540 meters.
The Tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo species, is critically endangered and found exclusively in the wild on Mindoro island.
Baguio City experiences a cooler climate than the rest of the country because it sits 1,500 meters above sea level.
